speaker: NARRATOR
text: It's a little late for tears, isn't it, Barbara? Even though you didn't know it was going to happen today, you've still had your whole life to prepare for it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Of course, you've gotten into the habit of not being prepared. And now it's a little late, isn't it?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You're a creature of habit, Barbara, we all are.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Unfortunately, not all of your habits are good ones. This was how your day started.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Started wrong.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Your neighbor, Helen, is a creature of habit, too.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But she got up when the alarm went off.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Because, Barbara, that's what she really had in mind when she said it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Helen has trained herself to know what she's going to do, in what order, and where the things are to do it with.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: She really doesn't have to think about it. She already knows what clothes she's going to wear today.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: As it turned out, it was a special day for Helen, too. But she makes a habit of being ready for special days. She starts by having a place for things and keeping them there.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: She uses taste in selecting her clothes.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But more than that, she keeps them clean and mended.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And she's able to match the right skirt with the right sweater.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: This was going to be a special day for you.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But you hadn't gotten very far with your preparations for it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Was your whole family asleep?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: No, your mother was up. Had been for an hour.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Barbara!

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Barbara, get up! You'll be late for school!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Does she have to do this every morning, Barbara?

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Barbara, do you hear me?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: If your mother stopped acting like a second alarm clock for even one day, you'd probably think it was a dirty...

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Pete's sake, I hear you! I'm up!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You didn't seem at all appreciative.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Even if you're not really well -mannered, you could make a habit of being civil.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And you weren't really up when your mother called you.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Little lies are such a firm foundation for big ones.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You started your day with no plan at all.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Looking for your hairbrush?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Can't remember where you left it?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You forgot other important things today. Okay.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You meant to fix that collar, but you've gotten into the habit of putting things off. There are so many things you plan to do this coming Saturday or the one after that.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Let's see. You found the algebra notebook you lost.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The ski pants you meant to put away in the chest.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The afghan you started to knit last summer.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And, oh yes, the sweater you were looking for.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You decided to cover the spots on your sweater with a scarf.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You often do that, but you can't forget that the spots are there.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: If you had a habit plan for your mornings, you might get off to a decent start someday.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Helen has a habit plan, and it includes a healthy breakfast and a pleasant word with her parents.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: All three always enjoyed Mr. Elliott's comments on the news.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: It was time to get started for office and school.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Helen's dad would drop her on the way downtown.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And who could ask for a nicer way to go to school?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Your brother was ready, but your father couldn't wait for you.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Or you could have driven to school with him.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: He used to enjoy that drive too.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Your eggs were cold this morning, but you had no time to be picky about food or to think about your diet.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: No time for milk or even to say good morning.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: No time for manners.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You made a pretty picture with your rumpled skirt, your spotted sweater, and your hair in a tizzy.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: As usual, all your neighbors knew how late it was when you went by at your regular dog trot.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You were late for school this morning, but then you're almost always late, and you're guilty about it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: More so because your lateness is habitual.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You're in a rut with a bad habit, and the longer you stick with the habit, the deeper the rut gets.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: When you saw Helen, you suddenly felt envious.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But more than that, you felt a distaste for your sloppy ways. And you knew you could do something about them if only...

speaker: NARRATOR
text: That wasn't a happy thought, was it?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Or do you always drum with your fingers?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You were just chatting away with Helen when it happened. When the day suddenly turned into something special.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You've never been friends with Ann Tolliver, and you've always wanted to be.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Hi. Hi. Some of the crowd's coming over to my house right after school. Do you think you two could make it? Well, that'd be fun, Ann. I'd love to. Swell. Well, what do you say, Bobby?

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Sure, thanks. Okay, see you later. Bye.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: That'll be fun, won't it? Oh, yes. Nice.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Each school year sees new groups forming, old ones reforming. Yours is a changing social world, and the opportunities to be part of it must be taken when they arise.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You knew this afternoon that you were making a bad impression, and you knew how easy it is not to be invited again, and how quickly you can be left out of the crowd.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You were embarrassed by your messy hair and the fingernails you had neglected to clean.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You worried about the spots on your sweater, Barbara, but what really showed up were your habits.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You didn't find it very pleasant comparing yourself with the others.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: What? I said, what do you think?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You weren't listening.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You seldom do.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: It's a habit of yours.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: I guess I don't know much about it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: They were talking about a popular book.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: All your friends were interested, but you never got into the habit of reading books.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: The whole problem was that Claudia wanted to be free to do all the things she'd never been allowed to do. Well, that was her whole reason for leaving her family. And then she married back in the same kind of life. Well, that's why I think the book's stupid. Why couldn't she have seen...

speaker: NARRATOR
text: No, you added nothing to that conversation.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: The trouble with me is getting started. I always have to force myself to do new things. I'm the same way. I didn't even want to go to my first concert because I thought it would be too long -haired.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Oh, but the music is wonderful. I'm going to go to the whole series.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: My mother had to drag me to the museum.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: They have a wonderful costume exhibit there. I got an idea for a new dress. Oh, what kind?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You've never taken an interest in music or politics or art.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: We always go to the beach. Every year we take a cottage.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You've only been once.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: There's wonderful swimming and lots of boys. It's quiet where we go.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: And there are tennis courts at the hotels, too, and dances every weekend. That sounds grand. And it's just a short way to the city.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You couldn't help interrupting, could you? And you couldn't help stretching proof like a rubber band.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: We all like to talk about ourselves.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But a soliloquy isn't a conversation.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: First you didn't talk at all, and then you did all the talking.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Conversation is a two -way street.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But for you, it's either one way or a dead end.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Goodbye. I hope you had a very nice day. Oh, thank you. I did. Bye. See you tomorrow.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: You too, George, you say? Thank you.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: In all society at all ages, we know that people are going to talk about other people.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Unfortunately, our faults are often more discussed than our good points. And sometimes our good points are completely hidden by our faults. But perhaps worst of all is our own disappointment in ourselves and the remarks we imagine our friends are making about us.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: Gee, I think dirty fingernails are horrible.

speaker: CHARACTERS
text: They're not sharp.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: A spotted sweater isn't shyness. And bad manners are still bad manners no matter what you call them.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Now in your own room, the memory of this day stands between you and your whole pattern of behavior.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Where will you start?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Your complexion?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: That starts with soap and water and goes on to regular meals and the right kind of food.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Your hair?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: It's more than just a shampoo, when you happen to think of it. Your clothes?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Not just cleaned when your mother takes them away from you, but a system of cleaning.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: For all a pattern, a network of habits.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Helen checks her clothes for cleaning when she takes them off. That's a habit of hers.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: This morning, Helen took her skirt from the front of the closet. Tonight, she hangs it in the back.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: That's a habit, too.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: One on the plus side.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: It gives clothes a chance to hang, rests the fabric.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Tonight, Helen makes a plan for tomorrow.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: A what to wear, what to do, when to do it, designed for living.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Helen has the habit of being ready for special days.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Good habits save time and energy and give us greater freedom to do those extra things we want to do.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Yes, a good start, but these improvements are not yet habits, not by any means.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: They must happen again and again until they fit into the fabric of the days without conscious thought. If you try, really try, you can root out the poor accidental habits and establish in their place the good habits approved by custom, accepted by society.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Across the street, Helen's light goes out.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Reasonable hours are part of her pattern, and you, Barbara.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Well, you've had a hard day, but staying awake to think about it won't help it any.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Go to bed early for a change.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Give yourself a good start on a new day.
